title: Find the largest element in an array (keep a variable `max`, update it when you find something bigger).
shortTitle: Find the largest element in an array
keyPoints: Seed a max variable with the first element, then scan the rest of the array once and update max whenever a larger value appears.
The algorithm runs in O(n) time because every element is visited exactly once, and O(1) extra space because only one tracking variable is used.
You cannot do better than O(n) because skipping any element risks missing the largest.
For money always use BigDecimal and compare with compareTo, never double and the greater-than operator.
Guard the empty array by throwing IllegalArgumentException rather than returning a misleading zero.
Seeding with the first real element is safer than seeding with zero or Integer.MIN_VALUE, especially when all values could be negative.

s1_definition.oneliner: Start by assuming the first element is the biggest, then walk the array once and upgrade max whenever something larger appears.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Linear scan** – you visit each element exactly once from left to right, so the algorithm is O(n) time.
- **Tracking variable** – a single variable `max` remembers the biggest value seen so far, giving O(1) extra space.
- **Seeding** – initialise `max` with the first element, not with zero, because amounts can be negative debits.
- **Comparison** – for `BigDecimal` use `compareTo` where a positive result means the left value is larger, because `BigDecimal` does not support the `>` operator.
- **Edge case** – an empty array has no largest element, so throw `IllegalArgumentException` rather than returning a misleading value.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh wants to know the single biggest deposit he made all year at National Bank of India. He takes his passbook, points at the first deposit and says "this is the biggest so far." Then he reads each later deposit one by one. Every time he sees a deposit bigger than the one he is pointing at, he moves his finger to that new bigger one. When he reaches the end, his finger is on the biggest deposit of the year.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Finding the largest element in an array is a classic linear scan problem that I solve in a single pass with constant extra space. I seed a maximum variable with the first element of the array, and then I walk through the rest of the array, comparing each element with my current maximum and upgrading the maximum whenever I find something bigger. By the time I reach the end, the maximum variable holds the largest value.

In my banking project at National Bank of India, I used exactly this pattern to show a customer their highest single transaction for the month on their statement page. Rajesh's account SAV2001 has a list of transaction amounts, and I scan that list to find the biggest one. Because this is money, I store every amount as a BigDecimal and compare using the compareTo method, where a positive result means the left value is larger, since BigDecimal does not support the plain greater-than operator.

One nuance I always mention is the empty case. If the account has no transactions for the month, there is no largest value to return, so instead of returning a misleading zero I throw an IllegalArgumentException with a clear message. That way the calling code knows there was genuinely no data rather than believing a zero-rupee transaction occurred.

The seeding choice matters too. I seed with the first real element rather than zero, because a debit-only view could contain only negative amounts and seeding with zero would give a wrong answer that is not even in the array. This small guard is the difference between toy code and production code in a financial system.

Remember one sentence: seed max with the first element, scan once, and update whenever you find something bigger.
